quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: The traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means you should slow down and stop before the intersection if it is safe. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the bridge or overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.explanation: This sign means an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Give pedestrians the right-of-way when they are crossing in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a pedestrian crossing ahead. Watch for people in the crosswalk and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is faster than is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current road conditions.

questions.explanation: You must drive at a safe speed for the area, traffic, weather, and road conditions. You must also obey posted speed limits.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
The driver who arrives last has the right-of-way.
One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: All vehicles must stop at a four-way stop. The first vehicle to arrive goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means:

options.text: Stop and look, then go if it is safe.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: Your tires lose grip when you drive too fast on wet roads. The tires cannot clear water from the road surface, causing the vehicle to slide on water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, do not panic. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the pavement. Keep both hands on the wheel and use a small steering movement. Check for traffic before steering back onto the road.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two-way traffic is coming.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you can check your blind spots by:

options.text: Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers to watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is starting. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and approaching a heavy truck from behind. You should know that:

options.text: The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles often travel slower than the posted speed limit, especially on hills. Be cautious when approaching a large truck from behind. On a hill with poor visibility, passing another vehicle is illegal.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers traffic rules they must obey. This sign shows the slowest speed you may drive. Do not drive below the posted minimum speed.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic may enter the road from a side road ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits U-turns. Do not make a U-turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: A driver should be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They're difficult to see in traffic.
They obey different traffic laws than larger motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They're difficult to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: In many crashes with motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians, drivers said they were looking but did not see them. These road users are harder to spot because they are smaller, move faster, and have less noticeable lights. Always watch carefully for motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians to prevent crashes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill section is coming.

questions.question: You are driving at night and a vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On either high or low beam.

questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when a vehicle is coming toward you or when you are following another vehicle at night. Use low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require you to slow down and pay attention.

questions.explanation: Work zones can be in one place or moving (like vehicles painting lines or removing snow). They have orange signs with black letters. Always slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. You must slow down when approaching the intersection and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if necessary.

questions.question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning, you should drive:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: If a driver feels worried, nervous, angry, or upset, they should:

options.text: Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can distract you from driving safely. Calm yourself and focus on the road before you start driving.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights flashing. You must:

options.text: Slow down. Change lanes if possible to stay away from the vehicle.
Move to the right side and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. Change lanes if possible to stay away from the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, slow down and change lanes if safe. If you cannot change lanes, slow down well below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much space as possible.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following except:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, the time between drinks, and your weight. It does not depend on the type of drink, how fit you are, or how well you think you can handle alcohol.

questions.question: When it starts raining, you should:

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit.
Drive close behind the car ahead of you.

questions.explanation: When rain makes it hard to see, slow down. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see well, pull to the shoulder and stop until it clears.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: You are entering a reduced speed zone.
You are leaving a reduced speed zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are leaving a reduced speed zone.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the times shown on the sign. The "End school zone" sign shows where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal means the same thing as:
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red signal, you must stop. Then yield to all traffic that does not have to stop.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from certain lanes. A green arrow means:

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may only proceed if a green arrow and a circular green light both appear.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. But you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign shows there are multiple lanes for left turns. Drivers in the far left lane must turn left.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your brain's control of judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time and hurts your coordination and balance. It also harms your vision and your ability to judge distance.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to warn other drivers. Look for other drivers who may also be moving into your lane.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means large trucks are not allowed where it is posted.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and drive through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Wait for that vehicle to pass safely before you go.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what other drivers are doing, even if it goes against the flagger's instructions.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal traffic laws as if there is no construction.

questions.explanation: Slow down and follow directions from signs, flaggers, or police in construction zones. Not doing so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:

options.text: May turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
Cannot turn and must go straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer need to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in the arrow's direction. But you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before you start the car, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: How should you safely cross a railroad?

options.text: Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways. Cross only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly go under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways. Cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. Watch for signals that show a train is coming. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When you turn right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When you turn, you must let other cars and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: A driver entering a highway from an entrance ramp:

options.text: Must let drivers already on the highway go first.
Can force their way into traffic.
Can expect other drivers to move for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must let drivers already on the highway go first.
questions.explanation: If you are entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you must let drivers already on the highway go first. Merge safely when you have a safe gap.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and hurts your ability to drive safely. It makes your reaction time slower and your judgment worse.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when it rains.

questions.question: When stopped by police or at a vehicle check, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must have your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times when driving. You must show all three documents if stopped.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign is at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you that you cannot drive in this direction.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than daytime driving because:

options.text: It is harder to see in the dark.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is harder to see in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far or as well. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough so you can stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Making it hard to focus on driving.
Lowering your chance of an accident.
Making you fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making it hard to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect how well you drive. Worry, anger, fear, excitement, or sadness can hurt your focus. Stress makes it harder to concentrate on driving safely. It is better to wait before driving if you are upset.

questions.question: You see a railroad crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Approach with care and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio so you can hear an approaching train.
Only cross after a flagger clears you, if one is present.

questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with care. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. Listen for trains and obey any flagger's directions.
